correctness.rationale: The word count is choose(6,3)*2^6=1280. Reverse-complementation preserves the two symbol classes; a fixed word contributes an even count from each class via the three paired positions, so none of the weight-three words is fixed. A closed code thus consists of entire two-word orbits. Vertex admissibility checks self-overlaps and overlaps within the orbit; edges check both directions between all words in the two distinct orbits. These conditions are equivalent to the stipulated all-ordered-pair condition, so an exact maximum clique of size 22 proves the maximum 44. The source's greedy coloring bound is valid on every prefix (a clique uses at most one vertex of each independent color class). Branching in reverse order on the greatest remaining vertex partitions improving cliques, retaining all earlier neighbors and pruning only via that bound. An independently written verifier reproduced 640 total orbits, 248 admissible orbits, 9048 edges and clique number 22, and checked the actual supplied 44 distinct words for exact weight, involution closure and every overlap direction and length. Replay `python3 /workspace/branches/f70bcbe1-e5e9-481a-9c21-ed89968bbfb7/independent_check.py`; see `independent_check.log` there. The verification had a different recursion order, so its node count is not the original's. The supplied source code was inspected, not executed. This is an exact finite combinatorial certificate, not a proof about longer words or properties of physical strands.

value.rationale: Balance, setwise involution closure, and synchronization via all proper overlaps are independent natural constraints on codes. Length six gives a short nontrivial even balanced case with only two-element orbits, unlike regimes that allow fixed words; it exposes the exact cost of imposing strand closure on the balanced optimum rather than merely ruling out a few examples. The sharp value and its attainment give a concrete benchmark for future constructions and bounds. No biochemical performance is claimed.
